original_question: Does every triangular billiard, or more generally every polygonal billiard, contain at least one periodic orbit?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It identifies the right object class (triangular billiards, with the paper's parenthetical extension to polygonal billiards) and the right property (existence of at least one periodic orbit). It also stays on the exact open problem rather than drifting to nearby questions such as mixing or escape.
missing_details: The ambient model should be made explicit: the paper uses the standard planar mathematical billiard, i.e. a point particle moving at constant speed in a compact polygonal domain D ⊂ R^2 with mirror-like (specular) reflection at the boundary.
The question is about closed polygonal billiards, not about an open billiard with a hole; it appears inside a review on open billiards because the closed polygonal case is a prerequisite difficulty.
The quantifier is existential over phase space: the problem asks whether there exists at least one periodic trajectory somewhere in the billiard, not whether every initial condition is periodic.

No direction is fixed in advance. The paper explicitly warns that some rational polygonal billiards have particular directional flows with no periodic trajectories, so the open problem is not a fixed-direction question.
To be fully stand-alone, 'periodic orbit' should be interpreted as exact recurrence to the initial state after finitely many reflections, i.e. return to the same position and direction.
The intended scope is finite planar triangles/polygons; nearby remarks about infinite rational polygonal billiards are only background, not part of Problem 11.5.
The nearby context notes known positive cases such as rational and acute triangles, so the unresolved content is the full triangle/polygon case beyond those special families.
refined_question: In the usual closed planar billiard system of a point particle moving in a compact polygonal domain D ⊂ R^2 with mirror-like reflections at the sides, does every triangular billiard—and, more generally, every polygonal billiard—admit at least one periodic trajectory, meaning a trajectory that after finitely many reflections returns to its initial position and direction, with no direction prescribed in advance?
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly Problem 11.5 in the polygonal-billiards part of Section 11.4, and your draft already matches it almost verbatim. The only needed sharpening is to make explicit the ambient billiard model, the fact that the problem concerns existence of some periodic orbit in the full billiard flow rather than in a chosen directional flow, and the paper's later description of periodic orbits as exact recurrence to the initial state. I therefore kept the triangle-first wording from the paper, retained the paper's own parenthetical extension to polygonal billiards, and avoided replacing it by the neighboring mixing problem or by a broader question about all directional flows.
